summary: AstroPilot is now NightSeam: new name, and the website has moved to nightseam.de. Planning and the image library work exactly as before. If you replace an older installation in place, rename data/astropilot.db to data/nightseam.db to keep your sites and captures.

Reliability release: a failed backup import can no longer wipe your data, planning now resolves the correct night at every location (timezone fix), safer panorama handling, and many small fixes in both apps.
Targets are ranked with community popularity as a silent tiebreaker, and moon-aware scoring now accounts for the Moon's phase, your filters and your sky brightness (Bortle class).
The web setup wizard is centred correctly, more controls carry proper accessibility labels, and the library and panorama handling got small fixes.
Better keyboard and screen-reader support (dialog roles, focus traps, labelled search), smoother handling of very large imports, and internal cleanups.
Safer backup import (a safety copy is written before anything is replaced), streamed uploads that no longer need the whole session in memory, and small web fixes.
The session journal was removed from both versions — planning and the image library are unchanged, but observed marks and journal notes are gone.
Horizon photos now survive reloading the page, and the “free space” layout setting works on any screen.
More stable time slider; changing the minimum altitude no longer flashes the target list.
Public release: open source (MIT), credits and notices, automatic update checker in the desktop app, download page.
Target grades (S–D) in the desktop app; weather with a 4-day forecast in both versions; new website.
Target grades (S–D) for the web; the sky map zoom now opens a wider rectangular view.
New interface: hamburger menu, Glass theme, desktop-style layout in the browser.
Web version: sites, rigs, custom targets and first-run setup.
The web version joined the project.
